body.x: CUBIC-K (CEO Kim Dongchoul) participated in CES Unveiled, a global media event held on January 5 (local time) ahead of CES 2025's official opening. The company specializes in providing solutions that utilize Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) and AI-based signal analysis technology to enable non-destructive and real-time analysis of complex mixtures within samples. According to the company, this allows for precise measurement of specific substances’ concentrations, significantly reducing errors and enhancing productivity in bioreactor research.

At the Unveiled event, CUBIC-K introduced its Quantix solution, which integrates SERS and AI technology for high-sensitivity detection and real-time automated monitoring. Due to its rapid and accurate analysis capabilities, the company emphasized its broad applicability across research and industrial sectors.

Quantix’s technological distinction lies in its machine learning-based signal preprocessing, which ensures consistent and reliable signal measurements. The company’s expertise in designing metallic nanostructures that amplify Raman scattering signals makes this possible, enabling precise concentration analysis tailored to diverse customer needs.

Additionally, the AI software embedded within Quantix automates and streamlines data generation and real-time monitoring, presenting intuitive numerical outputs for user convenience. These features simplify data acquisition and interpretation, making the product accessible to non-specialist users and seasoned researchers.

CUBIC-K’s innovative Quantix solution earned the CES 2025 Innovation Award in the "Industrial Equipment and Machinery" category, demonstrating the product’s technological excellence and market competitiveness.

body.cap: CUBIC-K representatives introduced the Quantix solution to AVING News reporter Alex Sigrist during CES 2025 Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: According to a company representative, "Quantix's analysis technology surpasses the limitations of traditional methods like liquid chromatography, offering unmatched functionality and ease of measurement. Its mechanism eliminates the need for separate sampling processes, dramatically reducing time and effort across research workflows and enabling researchers to undertake more processes within shorter timeframes, thereby significantly enhancing productivity."

The representative added, "We are thrilled to present Quantix, our next-generation measurement solution, at CES Unveiled, where global media converge. This opportunity allows us to highlight our product’s advantages and features to an international audience before the main exhibition begins. We hope to create even more opportunities in the upcoming days of CES 2025."

CUBIC-K participated in CES 2025 as part of the Seoul Pavilion in Eureka Park, the startup-focused exhibition area. The Seoul Pavilion, expanded by over 50% from the previous year to 1,040 square meters, featured 104 startups. It represents a collaboration between three Seoul districts (Gangnam, Geumcheon, and Gwanak), five startup support organizations (SBA, Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul AI Hub, and Campus Town Growth Center), and eight universities (Konkuk, Kyung Hee, Kookmin, Dongguk, Sogang, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Yonsei, and Chung-Ang).
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
